title: Feeding Our Future: The $120,000 Juror Bribe That BACKFIRED
summary:
Feeding Our Future juror bribe: on June 2, 2024, during the first Feeding Our Future fraud trial in Minnesota, a courier delivered $120,000 in cash in a Hallmark gift bag to the home of Juror 52, with a promise of more for a not-guilty vote. Juror 52 reported it to the police. According to federal prosecutors, $200,000 had been collected for the bribe — the courier, Ladan Ali, kept $80,000 for herself. All five people charged pleaded guilty to bribery of a juror. On November 20, 2026, Ali became the last to be sentenced: 4 years in prison. Abdiaziz Farah got 120 months on top of 28 years for the fraud; Said Farah 6½ years (he had been acquitted of the fraud in 2024); Abdimajid Nur 5 years on top of 10 for the fraud; Abdulkarim Farah 57 months.
Feeding Our Future, juror bribery, Juror 52, Abdiaziz Farah, Ladan Ali, Abdimajid Nur, Said Farah, Minnesota fraud, $250 million pandemic fraud.
No photographs of the defendants are shown. Exhibit images are government trial exhibits reproduced in a public court filing (D. Minn. 22-cr-124, Dkt. 929).

Quotes from hearings are as reported by MPR News, KSTP and the AP.
question: Juror 52 called the police. The courier who skimmed $80,000 got 4 years; the man prosecutors called the organizer got 10 on top of 28. Was 4 years enough? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: The courier kept $80,000 of the bribe for herself and got 4 years. The man prosecutors called the organizer got 10 more years on top of 28. Who deserved the most time?
